modmenu.descriptionTranslation.inventory: Organizes your inventory with configurable slot rules, kits, and storage presets.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.title: Tutorial
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s1.head: Welcome
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s1.caption: Hi there! Inventory Organizer packs in a LOT of features, which is exactly why it can feel a bit overwhelming the first time you open it. Sit back and relax - this short walkthrough goes through the important parts one at a time, with real examples. You don't need to click anything; just watch, and you can replay it later from the Guide whenever you like.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s2.head: Assign one exact item
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s2.caption: Let's say you want THIS particular slot to always hold your pickaxe, no matter what else is in your inventory. Click the slot to select it, then search for the exact item name on the right-hand panel and place the Diamond Pickaxe there. From now on, only that exact item is allowed to land in this slot - right-click it anytime to reset it back to 'any' if you change your mind.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s3.head: Don't know the name?
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s3.caption: Not sure of the exact name or ID? No problem at all - open the Names screen from the main menu. Every single item in the game is listed there in alphabetical order, together with its exact ID, so you can always find precisely what you're looking for.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s4.head: Or let it be automatic
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s4.caption: Prefer things to happen automatically instead? Simply take the exact item back out and leave a plain 'pickaxe' rule in the slot. From this point on, the mod itself decides WHICH pickaxe should go here whenever you sort - and that decision is made using the Ranks system, which we'll look at next.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s5.head: Ranks: three big criteria
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s5.caption: Ranks is built from three separate criteria, and YOU choose the order they're checked in: Materials, Enchantments, and Durability. Whichever one you put on top completely overrides the ones underneath it - so the order really matters, as you're about to see.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s6.head: Materials on top
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s6.caption: Picture two pickaxes sitting in your inventory: a well-used Netherite one, already at half durability, with just Efficiency on it - and a brand-new Diamond one, at full durability, enchanted with Mending. With Materials sitting on top of the list, the Netherite wins and takes the slot every time. Its material simply outranks everything else, even though the Diamond pickaxe is objectively in better shape and has the stronger enchantment.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s7.head: Enchantments on top
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s7.caption: Now let's reorder things and put Enchantments on top instead. This time the Diamond pickaxe wins: Mending simply ranks higher on the enchantment priority list than Efficiency does. Durability happens to agree here too, so either way you look at it, the Diamond comes out on top in this particular example. And just like the three main criteria, that enchantment priority list itself isn't fixed - you can freely reorder which enchantments matter most to you, right there in Ranks.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s8.head: Two slots? Use Tier
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s8.caption: But what happens when TWO slots both want a pickaxe at the same time? That's where the Tier number on every slot rule comes in. If both slots share the same tier, the earlier one (the lower-numbered slot) always takes the higher-ranked pickaxe - fixed and predictable, never random, even though it might look that way at first glance. Give the two slots different tiers instead - say Tier 1 and Tier 2 - and the higher-ranked pickaxe will always land in the Tier 1 slot. In short: the better an item ranks, the better (lower-numbered) tier slot it ends up in.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s9.head: Linked chests
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s9.caption: Here's something really useful: link several chests together, and they'll all sort as if they were one single, big warehouse - using the exact same Tier logic you just saw for individual slots. One heads-up though: this particular part depends heavily on the server you're playing on and is genuinely hard to test in every possible situation, so there's a chance some rare, edge-case bugs we don't know about yet could still show up here.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s10.head: Bundles are profile-based
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s10.caption: Bundles work quite differently from everything else: you never pick which physical bundle gets what directly. Instead, you create profiles - essentially describing what a bundle SHOULD hold - and the mod pairs each profile up with an actual bundle for you. If you have one bundle but two profiles set up, the profile you created first always wins that pairing. If you have two bundles and two profiles instead, each bundle simply gets matched with one profile each.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s11.head: Potions & group ranks
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s11.caption: Potions use exactly the same slot-rule system you've already seen - just place a potion rule on the slot you want. And here's a nice bonus: inside any custom group you build yourself (say, a group made up of different seeds), Ranks also lets you order the individual members against each other, so your personal favourite always ranks the highest within that group.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s12.head: Quick reference
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s12.caption: Here's a handy cheat sheet covering all three ways the rank order can decide between our two pickaxes. Important: being first in the list doesn't mean the other criteria are ignored - it just means that one gets the first say, and only hands the decision off to the next one in line when it's tied. Bundles follow the exact same logic - best content match wins first, and any leftover bundle profiles pair up with empty bundles in the order you listed them.
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s13.head: That's it!
inventory-organizer.tutorial.s13.caption: And that's really the gist of how Inventory Organizer thinks! Everything you just saw is available and adjustable from the main config screen, and you can always replay this whole tutorial again later from the Guide, whenever you need a refresher. Have fun with it - and happy organizing! Keep in mind this is a helper, not magic - it won't always get everything perfectly right, and there may still be bugs we're working out. If you spot one, please report it at https://github.com/Zefryxis/InOr/issues so we can fix it.

inventory-organizer.warehouse.help_body:
§eWhat is this?§r A warehouse links several chests into one store.

§b• Click§r chests on the map to select them (gold = selected).
§b• Link§r joins 2+ nearby chests (max 15 blocks) into one group.
§b• OST§r at ANY linked chest then sorts the WHOLE group: every
   item flies to the chest whose profile wants it most.
§b• Unlink§r removes the selected chests from their group.
§b• Sort§r sorts just the selected chests right now.

§7Scroll to zoom. A double chest counts as one; stacked chests
§7fan out with a §ey<level>§7 badge. Only chests you have opened
§7appear; chests without a profile stay hidden.

inventory-organizer.onboarding.title: Choose your setup
inventory-organizer.onboarding.intro: How much do you want to customize? You can change this anytime in Special Settings.
inventory-organizer.onboarding.simple_de: One ready-made system. Only slot rules, bundles and basic toggles. Easiest to understand - best if you're new.
inventory-organizer.onboarding.advanced_: Adds custom groups and slot-tier (ranks) editing. Step up once Simple feels familiar.
inventory-organizer.onboarding.expert_de: Everything is customizable - the full experience. For when you know the mod well.
inventory-organizer.special.mode_confirm: These levels aren't arbitrary - Inventory Organizer can do a LOT, so the options are layered so you can grow into them:
§aSimple§r - only the essentials: slot rules, bundles and basic toggles. Sorting and groups run on sensible built-in defaults.
§eAdvanced§r - adds custom groups and slot-tier (rank) editing, so you decide what goes where. Deep sort tuning stays on defaults.
§cExpert§r - everything is exposed: sort priority, material/enchant/potion order, the lot. Powerful, but a lot to take in.
Switching to %s. A lower level only HIDES options - nothing is deleted, and it all returns the moment you raise the level again.
inventory-organizer.guide.welcome.head: Welcome
inventory-organizer.guide.welcome.t1: Everything Inventory Organizer can do. Scroll to read; click Back when done.
inventory-organizer.guide.welcome.d1: Most automatic features only work in 'Free' mode: single player, LAN, Realms, Aternos, or a server you whitelisted. On normal public servers they stay off (safe).
inventory-organizer.guide.slots.head: Slot rules (Inv tab)
inventory-organizer.guide.slots.t1: Left-click a slot after picking a rule from the right panel = assign that rule.
inventory-organizer.guide.slots.t2: Right-click a slot = reset it to 'any'.
inventory-organizer.guide.slots.t3: Double-click a slot = open Tier Order for fine sort priority.
inventory-organizer.guide.slots.d1: 'any' accepts anything · 'empty' is kept empty by the sorter.
inventory-organizer.guide.refill.head: Auto-refill (the green R)
inventory-organizer.guide.refill.t1: Middle-click a HOTBAR slot = mark it for auto-refill (a green R badge appears).
inventory-organizer.guide.refill.t2: In Free mode, when that slot empties it is refilled automatically from the rest of your inventory — pickaxe, block, anything.
inventory-organizer.guide.refill.d1: Refill uses the slot's rule if it has one (e.g. any sword), else the last item there. Works in both Plain and Auto-switch modes.
inventory-organizer.guide.chestrefill.t1: Open a chest and press 'Rf' (or the Chest refill keybind): every marked hotbar slot is topped up with a matching stack FROM the chest.
inventory-organizer.guide.deposit.head: Deposit (Dep button / scroll)
inventory-organizer.guide.deposit.t1: Press 'Dep' in a chest to return every inventory stack whose item already belongs there. Scroll up over any inventory slot while a chest is open to deposit just that item.
inventory-organizer.guide.deposit.d1: Both methods are OST-aware: if the profile has a slot rule for that item and the slot is free, the item goes there instead of a random free chest slot. (Free mode.)
inventory-organizer.guide.sorting.head: Sorting: OST / OI
inventory-organizer.guide.sorting.t1: OST = sort the open chest. OI = sort your inventory (including items in your offhand).
inventory-organizer.guide.sorting.t2: Same items merge into full stacks and identical types are grouped together.
inventory-organizer.guide.sorting.d1: The Sort keybind does OST when a chest is open, else OI (configurable in Special).
inventory-organizer.guide.potions.head: Potion slot rules
inventory-organizer.guide.potions.t1: Give a slot a potion rule (e.g. Fire Resistance) and it accepts that effect in all three bottle types — drinkable, splash and lingering.
inventory-organizer.guide.potions.d1: Ranks → 'Potion Type Order:' sets which bottle type is preferred when more than one is available.
inventory-organizer.guide.scroll.head: Scroll actions (Free mode)
inventory-organizer.guide.scroll.t1: Scroll up over a slot inside a chest = deposit it (OST-aware). Scroll down = loot to inventory. Scroll in your own inventory = quick-move.
inventory-organizer.guide.scroll.t2: Shift + scroll in your inventory = OI sort, one item per notch.
inventory-organizer.guide.trash.head: Trash / Void
inventory-organizer.guide.trash.t1: Under Storage, open 'Trash' and place item rules in the grid. In Free mode any matching item is dropped the moment you pick it up.
inventory-organizer.guide.trash.d1: Special Settings → 'Trash mode' switches Drop all / Keep 1 stack (drop only the excess).
inventory-organizer.guide.storage.head: Storage & per-chest profiles
inventory-organizer.guide.storage.t1: Storage = 3 built-in defaults + your saved per-chest profiles ('Profiles…'), plus the Trash editor.
inventory-organizer.guide.storage.t2: Open a chest → 'New profile?' → Yes makes that chest remember its layout.
inventory-organizer.guide.storage.d1: A sign next to a chest names its profile · the 'Pr' button re-binds a carried profile.
inventory-organizer.guide.groups.head: Groups, Tier Order, Kits
inventory-organizer.guide.groups.t1: Groups = fully editable item collections. The built-in groups (Weapons, Blocks, Food…) are real, complete groups built from the game's own data — open any to fine-tune its items.
inventory-organizer.guide.groups.t2: Tier Order = sort priority within a type. Kits = save/load whole slot-config presets.
inventory-organizer.guide.groups.t3: Keybind 'Cycle slot preset' switches between your saved Kits on the fly.
inventory-organizer.guide.special.head: Special Settings
inventory-organizer.guide.special.t1: Keybind mode: Inventory-only / Free / Off. Sort action: Smart / OI / OST / Both.
inventory-organizer.guide.special.t2: Death auto-sort re-sorts after you recover your gear. Whitelist is opt-in (at your risk).
inventory-organizer.guide.switch.head: Auto Tool Switch
inventory-organizer.guide.switch.t1: Enable 'Auto switch' mode in the Inv tab: designate one hotbar slot as the Switch slot and one or more inventory slots as storage. The mod automatically puts the right tool (pickaxe for stone, axe for wood, sword for mobs) into your Switch slot as you look around.
inventory-organizer.guide.switch.t2: Configure tool groups under Ranks -> switch categories. Each category (Pickaxe / Axe / Shovel / Hoe / Mob weapon) can be assigned a group -- Ranks picks the best item in that group. 'On air' sets what happens when you look at empty space: keep, restore the last item, or swap to a specific tool type.
inventory-organizer.guide.switch.t3: Trigger mode (Trigger button in the tab): 'Auto' swaps immediately whenever your crosshair target changes -- single player only. 'Button' mode works everywhere (servers too): press the 'Switch: Trigger Tool Swap' keybind to manually trigger the swap.
inventory-organizer.guide.switch.d1: In Auto mode the attack cooldown ticker counts up in your inventory so the tool is already ready when it reaches your hand.
inventory-organizer.guide.warehouse.head: Warehouse (multi-chest)
inventory-organizer.guide.warehouse.t1: The 'Wh' button / keybind opens a top-down chest map. Link nearby chests, then OST at any of them sorts the WHOLE group.
inventory-organizer.guide.warehouse.d1: On servers, only YOUR linked chests are visible; others can OST them only if you grant it (the 'OST' button on the map). Nobody can link or take from your chests.
inventory-organizer.guide.keybinds.head: Keybinds (Controls → Inventory Organizer)
inventory-organizer.guide.keybinds.t1: Sort · Open Kits · Open Settings · Open Warehouse map · Chest refill · Cycle slot preset · Toggle Auto-Refill.
inventory-organizer.guide.keybinds.d1: All unbound by default — assign the ones you want in the normal Controls menu.
inventory-organizer.hud.title: HUD Layout
inventory-organizer.hud.hint: Toggle elements on the right, then drag them onto the frame.
inventory-organizer.hud.resize: Scroll over an element to resize it.
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.head: Craft from nearby chests
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.t1: At a crafting table, the vanilla recipe book shows a recipe in green when nearby chests (ones you've opened) hold the missing ingredients.
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.t2: Click the recipe and the mod pulls the parts out of those chests and fills the 3x3 grid - ingredients you already carry are used too.
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.t3: A Materials panel sits beside the GUI, listing every nearby chest and its contents. Type to search, set 'Qty', then click any line to pull that item from that chest into your inventory.
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.t4: The slot under your inventory is a quick deposit: drop a held stack there to stash it in a nearby chest (auto-sorted). Click it empty-handed to send the whole crafting grid back - each ingredient returns to the chest it came from.
inventory-organizer.guide.crafting.d1: Chests are always checked first. Reach: 60 blocks in single player, 15 on servers.
inventory-organizer.guide.hud.head: On-screen HUD overlays
inventory-organizer.guide.hud.t1: Special -> 'HUD' opens the editor. Turn on the combat indicator, a 27-slot mini-inventory, and your worn gear (+offhand, with durability bars).
inventory-organizer.guide.hud.t2: Drag each element anywhere on the preview frame. Drag toward the middle and it snaps to the exact centre line (edge first, then centre).
inventory-organizer.guide.hud.t3: Scroll the mouse wheel over an element to resize it (50%-300%); the size shows on its label.
inventory-organizer.guide.hud.d1: Everything is off by default. The combat indicator only appears during real PvP combat.

inventory-organizer.guide.groups.d1: In Tier Order each group is a foldable section (▶/▼), closed by default — click a header to open it, then drag items to set which wins.
inventory-organizer.guide.groups.d2: Built-in contents: Blocks = full solid blocks only · Tools = mining tools plus usable items (ender pearl, buckets, lead…) · Weapons = swords, axes & ranged · Nether/End = everything from that dimension.
inventory-organizer.guide.fullinv.head: Full inventory
inventory-organizer.guide.fullinv.t1: Sorting handles a full inventory reliably. If an item truly has no free slot, you'll get a message naming it — free a slot, or set a Trash rule to auto-clear overflow.
inventory-organizer.sort.retry_failed: §eSorting hit a snag — try moving a few items, then sort again.
inventory-organizer.sort.no_room: §eNo room for %s — free up a slot, or set a trash rule to auto-clear.
